Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration This is an expedited recruitment process, open for applications from internal and internal-equivalent candidates only. Organizational Context and Scope IOM has been present in Myanmar since 2005 and is the leading intergovernmental organisation in the field of migration and works closely with governmental, intergovernmental, and non-governmental partners. IOM works to help ensure the orderly and humane management of migration, to promote international cooperation on migration issues, to assist in the search for practical solutions to migration problems, and to provide humanitarian assistance to migrants in need, including refugees, Internally Displaced People (IDP), victims of trafficking, stranded migrants, and other vulnerable migrants. As a result of the multifaceted crises faced in Myanmar in 2021, emergency and humanitarian needs have been increasing across the country. There has been an identified need for better data on population mobility, displacement, and multisectoral needs to support the humanitarian response. As such, IOM aims to support this effort through its Population Mobility and Needs Tracking (PMNT) programme. Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (COM) and the direct supervision of the Senior Programme Coordinator, the Programme Officer (Field Coordination) will be responsible and accountable for overseeing PMNT field implementation across Myanmar, ensuring the effective management and integration of data collection activities, field security, and administrative and financial support of field teams. Coordinate security-related aspects of field operations, including staff movements, daily tracking of field teams, and mission planning; develop and implement appropriate security risk mitigation measures; ensure compliance with security protocols and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) through regular training and oversight; and maintain effective coordination with security counterparts, local partners, and other stakeholders to support safe and secure programme implementation.
